title: The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order
main_claim: There is an absolute C with R(Q_n) ≤ C·2^n for all n (Theorem 1.1). The proof is by contradiction along a counterexample sequence with N/2^n → ∞ and N ≤ n2^n. Successive stabilized exclusions give initial discrepancy, then asymmetric discrepancy, then rule out intermediate bias, full-dimensional clusters and the linear-budget jump, which leaves deep discrepancy in both orientations. Patch extraction then splits into bounded, direct and cluster modes, each high or low, and every mode is excluded by an embedding.
coverage:
This is an assembly-level audit only; I did not re-audit section internals. I read the introduction, the regime guide, the regime table (including its exhaustion paragraph), proof-inputs.tex, the Reduction section (Lemma 2.1), and the final "Conclusion of Theorem 1.1" paragraph (18-late-dynamics:1313). I checked the statement and hypotheses of every result the chain invokes: Lemma 3.2 (stabilization); Lemma 4.1 (bias vs purity); Lemmas 5.1 and 6.1; the claim (eq:source-1); Lemma 7.1 and Corollary 7.2; Lemma 8.1 and Corollary 8.2; Definition 9.1 and Proposition 9.2, including its parameter-selection paragraphs; Proposition 10.1 and Corollary 10.2; Proposition 11.1 and Corollary 11.4; Corollary 12.1 and the constant order in §12 (R=P², L, u, ξ, θ, C_*); Definition 13.1 and Lemma 13.2; the §13 constant list, Proposition 13.3 and Lemma 13.4; the statements of Propositions 14.1 and 14.2; the statements of Lemma 15.1 and Propositions 15.3 and 15.4; the scale bounds at the head of §16 and Lemma 16.1; the uses of A_0 in §17; and Lemma 18.6 plus the final summation. I also built the cross-reference graph for all sections.

Results:
(a) Coverage of cases. H† is either below 1 or at least 1, and the case below 1 is excluded in either orientation (Prop 9.2, first bullet). Positivity of H inside the rectangle comes from Corollary 8.2, which needs x₂ < τ/4; that is arranged. Once both H† ≥ 1, H_L† lies in {0}, (0,1) or [1,∞]. The first is excluded by Prop 11.1: H_L† = 0 forces H_L(.01,.01) = 0 by monotonicity and nonnegativity. The second is excluded by Prop 9.2. The third gives deep discrepancy via Corollary 11.4, because H_L† is a supremum, so some rational point has H_L > h₀. In extraction, the order bounded → (g > M₁q ⇒ direct) → cluster is a full partition. A non-bounded case with g ≤ M₁q forces q ≥ Q₀, and a non-bounded direct case forces g ≥ M₁Q₀. Direct mode splits at K_B log n. Cluster mode splits at (log n)^{c_q} and at (log n)². The final paragraph's "high or low" covers all of these, with bounded counted as low direct.
(b) Hypotheses. In the side-swapped application of Lemma 6.1 in §7, the widths, the D₀ < D_*/2 cap and the defect exponent p₀ = c/2 all match. Corollary 7.2 feeds Lemma 7.1 with p = h/2 and widths ≤ n^{d/2}. Corollary 8.2 places the small-budget side as the odd side of Lemma 8.1 with β⁺ < τ/4. Lemma 13.2 builds a valid Proposition 10.1 witness: given a_C < min(η₀,1)/10⁶, there are rational ζ < γ′ and δ with γ′a_C < δ < min(η₀,ζ,1)/2000. The bound g ≤ n^{ι/2} uses (eq:source-9) at widths n^{a_B} with slack ι/2. In §16, the low-mode bounds M_i = N n^{-o(1)}, n|D−½| = O(log n), s_i = O(log n) and h_i ≤ (log n)^{.1} follow from c_q C_b < 1/20 and c_q M_lo < 1/20. High direct mode gets mass failure ≤ n^{-R} because s_i > 10⁻³K_B log n with K_B ≫ 10⁶R. The A_0 ≫ R slack covers both the Γ ≤ n^{-3R} bound and the palette-concentration count n^{2+o(1)}. The Hall sum needs only C_n → ∞ and e^{o(n)} patches; the paper's bound is #I ≤ e^{n^{2ι}}.
(c) Circularity. The dependency graph is acyclic: §5 → §6 → §7 → §8 → §9; §10 depends only on (eq:source-2); §11 depends on §9 and §10; §12 depends on §11; §§13–18 follow in order. The forward references in §5 and §10 are expository only.
(d) Constant order. η₀ → τ → per-pair exponents; then Definition 9.1 at rational parameters; then x_*, α; then P, R, L, u, ξ (< α2^{-10u-100}), θ, C_*; then ι, a_C, a_B; then M₁ (against C_*), C_b, M_lo, c_q, M_hi, ω; then a = θ/100, ρ; then K_B, A_0; then Q₀ last. No constant is chosen before something it depends on. Every stabilization step is applied to a countable list of rational-parameter properties, and the total removal is o(N).
sibling_notes:
Points worth a line-level check by the section reviewers, not assembly gaps:
(1) The §9 sublinear parameter choice requires χ < (1−y)/10 on the whole rectangle so that χ < σ/10 holds after σ is placed between 1−y_d and 1−y_s. This works, but only because χ is fixed before the diagonal subdivision.
(2) Lemma 13.4's own-patch degree test in cluster mode needs q^{C_b} > M₁q, i.e. q^{C_b−1} > M₁. This rests on the threshold Q₀.
(3) Direct-mode Γ ≤ K e^{-200s_i} 2^{-p(v)} in §17 is only sketched at assembly level ("degree gain absorbs patch-width, conflict and crossing factors"). The section-17 reviewer should confirm the margin: gain ≈ e^{-g/2}, against e^{.001g + g^{a_B}} and 2^{ℓ_i}.
(4) The final "Conclusion of Theorem 1.1" paragraph is terse, but every step it names is backed by a stated result.
